sn55.53:1.2: Despite his evident eminence, this is the only appearance of the layman Dhammadinna. For the nun of the same name, see [mn44](). | Other lay followers with similarly large retinues include Anāthapiṇḍika [an5.176:1.1](), Hatthaka of Āḷavī ([an8.24:1.2]()), and Dhammika ([snp2.14:1.3]()).
sn55.53:2.2: Such discourses, which are also referred to at [an2.47:1.5](), [an5.79:5.2](), and [sn20.7:2.4](), contrast with the frivolous poetry of outsiders. I take the expression as simply referring to the Suttas in general. | The expression “undertake and dwell” (_upasampajja viharati_) is normally used for meditation states, whereas for the Suttas one is enjoined to listen, scrutinize, and memorize. Perhaps the original intent was to “enter and dwell in the meditations taught in the Suttas”.
